tonight.headline: Send the Tuten offer. The one fact it was missing - whether Lamar Jackson is healthy in 2026 - came back today, and it is clean: 324 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1, no injury report, hosting a Saints defence that gave up 31 to Detroit.
body: First, discount the 76%. KEI returns have five starters set out of nine - no receivers, no defence, no kicker - which is why ESPN shows them at 70.8 against your 119.6. They were editing their lineup at 16:56 this afternoon and dropped Jason Myers for Evan McPherson at 16:56, so this is a manager mid-edit, not a manager who has quit. Expect that number to fall back toward even by Sunday. Do not plan around it.

The real news is that the Team 13 trade is now fully supported. For seven consecutive runs this deal has been priced on a seasonProj field with no reporting behind the player you are buying, and every brief said so. RotoWire's 13 September game report has Lamar Jackson at 17 of 25 for 324 yards and a touchdown, plus 7 carries for 40 and a rushing score - 13.0 yards per attempt, nine different receivers - with no injury attached to him. The only Baltimore injury in that report is Zay Flowers' hamstring.

Second: the Bowers trigger finally fired, and it fired the other way. Brock Bowers did not practise on Wednesday. RotoWire, today: Klint Kubiak hopes he can go Thursday or Friday, one week after a meniscus trim. The condition written on 14 September said 'limited or sits out Wednesday, keep Mayer through Week 2'. Keep Mayer. The Hockenson card is retired for this week, and FantasyPros independently list Mayer as the only Raiders pass-catcher with both end-zone and red-zone targets.

Third, and least welcome: Matthew Stafford is still on your bench and Trevor Lawrence is still in your starting slot, fourteen hours after this was called ELITE. It is worth +2.6 this week. I also tested the clause the morning brief could not test, and it passes - see below.

case.label: The falsification clause I could finally test
case.body: The Stafford card's own condition was 'Stafford appears on any Rams injury report'. This morning's brief could not check it and said so twice. I retrieved therams.com's own injury-updates page this run: the most recent entry is dated 14 September 2026 and concerns Myles Garrett having knee surgery and going to injured reserve, plus Kam Curl, Nate Landman, Davis Allen and Omar Speights. Stafford is not on it. The most recent Stafford injury item anywhere is an August 2025 preseason back issue. The clause does not fire.

case.label: What that page cost him elsewhere, which cuts the other way
case.body: The same page says Myles Garrett is done for a while. Los Angeles are 6th of 32 on DraftSharks' Week 2 board, and that ranking was earned with Garrett. A Rams front without its best pass rusher is a softer draw than the tile suggests - which helps Stafford's own matchup read very little, since he plays for them, but it is the kind of thing that should make you discount the LAR tile on any player facing them.

case.label: Why the trade is the headline and not the lineup swap
case.body: The swap is worth +2.6 this week. The trade is worth +11.6 to you on the season and +40.6 to Team 13, which is why it is the one with a real chance of being accepted. Re-run exhaustively on this snapshot - every one-for-one and every two-for-one across all nine opponents - it remains the best proposal available to you in this league, and Team 13's shape is unchanged: Josh Allen at slot 0 starting, Lamar Jackson at slot 20 on the bench, and Rachaad White at 164.6 leaking their second running back slot.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Baltimore's Thursday or Friday report adds Jackson - the 324-yard game is Week 1 evidence and a fresh report would outrank it. Or Team 13 start a second running back or move a quarterback, either of which removes the shape the offer is built on. Or the Rams add Stafford to Thursday's report, which voids the lineup card and returns Lawrence to your starting slot.

case.body: FantasyPros' Week 2 waiver column has Vele as New Orleans' clear number-two behind Chris Olave on a 90.7% snap share with 10 true targets in Week 1. case.body: He is 43.7% rostered nationally and his ownership moved +30.65 this week, the second-largest rise on your wire. In Chem he was already claimed at 07:14 this morning by JuiceJam. Here he is still sitting as a free agent, which is the why=OWNED band STRATEGY section 4 calls the strongest single wire signal in a shallow league. That gap does not usually last two days.

case.body: Status is FREEAGENT, not WAIVERS. STRATEGY section 6 is explicit that only claims consume priority, and IPADE priority never resets - you are 3rd of 10 and have spent none of it. This add is free in the only currency this league charges. Nothing clearing tonight justifies spending the real thing: the Rams defence at 91.2% rostered and Jake Ferguson at 82.6% are both genuine anomalies and both are streamers or a third tight end, which section 6 rules out by name.

Boutte appears nowhere in the 44-row activity log going back to 10 September, so he predates it. He is a replaceable flex body, which section 3 names as the thing that lowers the bar.

case.label: The two numbers side by side
case.body: Lawrence for McLaurin: you +13.1, Furia Regia +3.7. Stafford for McLaurin: you +8.7, Furia Regia +8.1. Both recomputed on this snapshot over full rosters, ignoring this week's kickoffs, per the trade rules. case.body: If the Team 13 deal lands first, the two versions become identical for you: selling either quarterback for McLaurin takes you to 2115.4 either way, +28.0 on top of the Lamar deal. Identical to you, +8.1 versus +3.7 to them. There is no version of this where Lawrence is the right chip once Lamar is in the building.

case.label: The pattern worth naming
case.body: Both errors have the same shape: the optimiser was asked what YOU gain and the answer was taken as the proposal. STRATEGY section 7 says compute both lineups and state their gain in the headline. Running the search over your own surplus and then picking your largest number is not the same computation, and it has now produced two unsendable offers in two days.

whatWentWrong.title: The Hockenson card sat on a practice report for three runs and the report, when it came, said no.
whatWentWrong.lead: A conditional card was carried on 14, 15 and 16 September waiting for Las Vegas to practise. They practised. Bowers did not, which under the card's own trigger means keep Michael Mayer - the opposite of what three runs of framing implied was coming.

case.label: What the trigger actually said, and what happened
case.body: Written 14 September: 'Bowers practises in full Wednesday or carries no designation Friday, then drop Mayer before week 2. Bowers is limited or sits out Wednesday, then keep Mayer through week 2.' RotoWire today, 16 September: Bowers will not practise Wednesday; Klint Kubiak hopes he can go Thursday and/or Friday; he is about a week out from a meniscus trim. Sat out. Keep Mayer.

case.label: Where the framing drifted from the trigger
case.body: This morning's card led with 'that is a club expecting him to play, which is the direction that ends Mayer's role' and promoted Hockenson from fallback to genuine flex candidate. Both may be true eventually; neither was the condition. A conditional card that spends three runs arguing for one branch is not neutral by the time the branch resolves, and this one had to resolve against its own momentum.

case.label: The fact that makes keeping Mayer positively good
case.body: Not merely the default. FantasyPros' Week 2 waiver column lists Mayer as a recommended pickup in his own right: the only Raiders pass-catcher with both an end-zone and a red-zone target, and the snap-share leader among them. Three runs treated him as a Bowers-shaped placeholder. He has a role.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Bowers practising in full on Thursday or Friday, or being listed without a designation on Friday - that is the second half of the original trigger and it is still live this week. If it fires, revisit Hockenson then; he is a free agent and costs no priority whenever you want him.

whatWentWrong.title: A trade recommendation named Terry McLaurin for two runs with no reporting behind him. There is reporting now and it is not flattering.
whatWentWrong.lead: Both briefs that proposed acquiring McLaurin said, in their own cannotSee sections, that they had never successfully researched him. I got him this run.

case.label: What he actually did
case.body: RotoWire, 13 September 2026: 2 catches on 4 targets for 14 yards against Philadelphia. Stefon Diggs took 9 targets in the same game. Rookie Antonio Williams also had 4. Jayden Daniels is throwing and RotoWire describe the distribution among Washington's new receiving group as an open question.

case.label: Why that matters more than a bad box score usually would
case.body: STRATEGY section 8 says weeks 1 to 3 are noise and to react to role news only. Target distribution sits on the line between the two: 14 yards is a box score and can be ignored, but being fourth in the pecking order behind Diggs is closer to role. STRATEGY section 7's buy-low rule wants strong underlying volume with bad results. McLaurin had weak volume AND bad results, which is not a buy-low, it is just a bad week that might be a bad role.

case.label: What I did with it
case.body: Kept the trade, repriced the chip, and cut the odds to EVEN. It still computes positive for both sides and the Dallas draw is the softest passing matchup on either board. But it is no longer a deal to chase, and this brief should not have been recommending a player it had never read a word about.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Washington's Week 2 usage restores McLaurin to the target lead - one game is a thin basis for a role call and the same RotoWire piece expects him to reassert himself. If that happens the odds go back up, not down.

The trigger's other branch is keep Mayer through Week 2, and FantasyPros independently make Mayer a recommended Week 2 add in his own right - the only Raiders pass-catcher with both an end-zone and a red-zone target.

case.label: Why he stays on the list anyway
case.body: 62.7% rostered nationally and free in a ten-team league is the why=OWNED anomaly STRATEGY section 4 rates highest. He runs 81% of Minnesota's routes as the second option behind Jefferson, and the quarterback question that hung over him is now settled in his favour: Carson Wentz is expected to start with Kyler Murray in concussion protocol, and Wentz threw Hockenson a touchdown in the Week 1 comeback. FantasyPros cite his rapport with Wentz explicitly. IPADE's flex takes a tight end, so he would not have to displace Loveland.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If Bowers practises in full Thursday or Friday, or is listed without a designation on Friday - the second half of the original trigger, still live this week. Or if Loveland posts a second consecutive blank. He is a free agent, so the move costs no priority whenever you decide, and that is precisely why it does not need to be made today.

worthALook.name: Pat Freiermuth
worthALook.lead: New this run, and the more interesting tight end on this wire than the one everybody is looking at.

case.label: The role fact
case.body: FantasyPros' Week 2 waiver column has him perfect on targets in Week 1 - five for five - with goal-line involvement, despite Pittsburgh's early-season pressure problems. Goal-line involvement at tight end is the scarcest thing on a waiver wire and it is the part of Colston Loveland's profile that is currently missing: Cole Kmet took the Bears' touchdown while Loveland caught nothing.

case.label: Why he is a note and not a move
case.body: You already carry two tight ends and the flex is spoken for by Golden. Adding a third means dropping Mayer, whom the Bowers trigger just told you to keep, or Loveland, which is a two-week overreaction to one blank. This is a name to hold for the moment Loveland's role is actually in question rather than merely disappointing.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A second Loveland blank on Sunday against Minnesota at 20th of 32 - a soft draw with nothing to show would be role evidence rather than script. Or Bowers returning in full, which frees the Mayer seat and makes this a straight swap rather than a three-tight-end problem.

doNotChase.name: Josh Allen
doNotChase.lead: The optimiser says asking Team 13 for Josh Allen gains you +16.9 and gains them +21.8. Re-run today, same answer. Still do not send it.

case.label: What the number is actually saying
case.body: The trade is Garrett Wilson for Josh Allen, and it clears the both-sides-gain test on this snapshot by a wide margin. The reason it clears is that the optimiser thinks Lamar Jackson backfills their quarterback slot for free, which is exactly the failure mode STRATEGY section 7 names by hand: 'The optimiser will occasionally propose trading an elite quarterback for a flex receiver because a backup appears to backfill the slot. It is always wrong.'

case.label: Why it is worse than that here
case.body: It also destroys the deal you actually want. Lamar is only available because he is redundant behind Allen. Take Allen and Lamar stops being surplus, which means the +40.6 offer on the table evaporates the moment this one is accepted. These two proposals cannot both exist, and the one worth +40.6 to them is the one that gets answered.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing this season. Section 7 makes any top-5 player at his position untouchable regardless of the maths, and Allen is analyst rank 1 at quarterback. This row exists so no future run rediscovers the number and treats it as new.

doNotChase.sources: recomputed on the 21:52 UTC snapshot · STRATEGY.md section 7

doNotChase.name: Jason Myers
doNotChase.ownership: 97.2% owned, on WAIVERS, clears Friday 07:00 UTC
doNotChase.lead: The single loudest ownership anomaly on your wire this week - 97.2% rostered and sitting there - and it is a trap because of what it would cost, not what he is.

case.label: Why he is available at all
case.body: KEI returns dropped him at 16:56 this afternoon to add Evan McPherson, which is visible in the activity log. That is a live-manager decision made ninety minutes ago, not a blunder that has been sitting for days, and it is the reason a 97%-rostered kicker is on your wire.

case.label: Why the price is wrong
case.body: His status is WAIVERS, clearing Friday at 07:00 UTC - so taking him costs your waiver priority, and IPADE priority never resets. STRATEGY section 6 spends two lines on this: priority goes to a player who starts immediately or a genuine league-winner, never a streamer, and a kicker is the definition of a streamer. You are 3rd of 10 and have spent nothing all season. Spending it on a kicker for +1.3 projected points would be the worst trade of the year.

case.label: The comparison you should make instead
case.body: Cam Little projects 8.1 against Denver. Cairo Santos is a FREE AGENT at 9.0. That is the move if you want a kicker upgrade, it costs nothing, and at +0.9 it is still under STRATEGY section 10's one-point floor - so the answer is hold Little for a sixth week.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: If Myers clears waivers unclaimed on Friday he becomes a free agent, and at that point he is a free comparison like any other. Until then the answer is no, and it is about the currency rather than the player.

doNotChase.sources: league activity log · league wire status and clearsAt · STRATEGY.md sections 5, 6 and 10

candidates.note: Devaughn Vele, WR NO, FREE AGENT at 43.7% rostered with ownership up 30.65 this week. Promoted to the doFirst card above; listed here so the reasoning survives if you do not act. FantasyPros have him as New Orleans' number two behind Chris Olave on a 90.7% snap share with 10 true targets in Week 1 - opportunity, which STRATEGY section 4 ranks first among all add signals. In Chem the equivalent manager claimed him at 07:14 this morning; here he is still free, which is the ownership anomaly and it will not last. Costs no waiver priority, which is the only currency this league charges.

Braelon Allen, RB NYJ, free at 13.6% rostered. New this run and recorded as the fallback if Vele is taken first. FantasyPros' Week 2 column describes him as a red-zone scoring threat complementing Breece Hall in a meaningful role - short-yardage work now rather than a handcuff waiting on an injury, which is the opposite of the Tuten profile you are trading away. Green Bay's defence at 7th of 32 makes this a hard week to debut him, so he is a hold-and-watch rather than a move.

Jordan Addison, WR MIN, rostered here by JuiceJam so not available to you - recorded because he is claimable in your other league tonight and the answer there is no, which is worth having written down once. FantasyPros have him at 96.3% route participation and ZERO targets in Week 1, in a game where Carson Wentz threw three touchdowns. Route share without targets is the most misleading number on any wire. If JuiceJam drop him, do not be the manager who picks him up on the ownership figure.
